title: dt/2 and a fresh seed for the phoretic division claim: halving the world's own step keeps division (10 persistent splits, generation 3 in 400 t vs 23 and 5 at dt, 1 and 1 with turnover off); seed 2 gives 14 persistent splits, generation 6
summary: The world of 20261026T0356-c33-phoretic-divide-claim, unchanged, run with screen.py and lineage.py (particle identity, persistence 20 t, merge-aware generations) for t=400. dt/2: WORLD_P {dt: 0.01, sub: 50} (the world's own Euler step halved, frame time and reaction step unchanged) on seed 0: 39 splits, 88 merges, 10 persistent, max generation 3, 8 of 10 leave B in both daughters (dthalf_seed0.png). At the default step seed 0 gave 49 / 89 / 23, generation 5, and the turnover-off twin 6 / 51 / 1, generation 1 (parent claim, lineage_particles.txt). Fresh seed 2 at the default step: 41 / 77 / 14, generation 6, 13 of 14 with B in both daughters (seed2.png). So division survives the halved step at about half the rate; the step affects how hard the B band is pulled, which suggests the split rate is not converged in dt.
